> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `sys_user (literal, 41 pages)`
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **143** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 71696121a64d8bd057fac969a72a84295890ed37` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `809fc5148dfc0010a09f0144757cb0c771f369c4` — the merge of head `38154076205504a920477219e862fd5a5b1630df` into base `71696121a64d8bd057fac969a72a84295890ed37`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 809fc5148dfc0010a09f0144757cb0c771f369c4 && git checkout 809fc5148dfc0010a09f0144757cb0c771f369c4
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 71696121a64d8bd057fac969a72a84295890ed37 38154076205504a920477219e862fd5a5b1630df && git checkout -B drift-repro 71696121a64d8bd057fac969a72a84295890ed37 && git merge --no-ff 38154076205504a920477219e862fd5a5b1630df

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 71696121a64d8bd057fac969a72a84295890ed37
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 71696121a64d8bd057fac969a72a84295890ed37` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `38154076205504a920477219e862fd5a5b1630df`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/field-value.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts + packages/lint/src/validate-object-references.ts, packages/lint/src/index.ts, packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-object-references.test.ts, packages/lint/src/object-graph.test.ts, packages/spec/src/data/field-value.test.ts, .changeset/24808-user-field-foreign-reference-warning.md; cited and read: packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (`DELETE_SEMANTICS_REFERENCE_TYPES`), packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts (`deleteBehavior` enum, `FieldSchema.reference`), packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-rule-service.ts (`fieldHoldsUsers`), packages/spec/src/data/default-value-shape.ts (`current_user`), packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts (`refuseForeignTreeReference`), packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts (reference suite `runtimeTypes`), docs/adr/0087-metadata-protocol-upgrade-contract.md (D2)

Reviewed at 2026-10-20T17:27Z · card #24808 (body and every comment, the claim `6294945987` and the os-dev-report `6296320062` included), decision card #24854 (body, director delta `6289564749`, triage record `6292049030`), the standing ruling 「甲」 (#6015 `6292005854`), PR #24942 body and file list, the net diff `origin/main...38154076` (merge-base `b42c621c05`, 9 files, +273/-6), and the check-runs on the head. Head repo is `objectstack-ai/objectstack` (not a fork). Nothing was built, run or re-run locally.

### ① Derived judgments

The diff implies the following accept-set and public-surface changes. Each is named right or wrong against the card's ruling (A on #24854, timed by 「甲」).

1. **Parse accept set of `ObjectSchema` / `FieldSchema` / `ObjectExtensionSchema`: unchanged.** No refinement is added; `FieldSchema.reference` stays `z.string().optional()`. `{ type: 'user', reference: 'probe_account' }` still parses, and the new `[#24808]` describe pins exactly that (`ObjectSchema.safeParse(...).success === true`). **Right** under 「甲」 rule 2: no conversion can carry the refusal (see item 5), so the 18.x half is loud only. No silent narrowing.
2. **Runtime resolution `referenceTargetOf` for `user`: unchanged** (still authored carrier first, `IMPLICIT_REFERENCE_TARGETS` as the fallback). Only the docblock on `IMPLICIT_REFERENCE_TARGETS` moves, and `field-value.test.ts` keeps the `my_people` pin with a comment naming it a protocol-18 pin. **Right.** The dispatch's step-3 sentence ("either way, `referenceTargetOf` for `user` returns `sys_user`") predates the derivation and is wrong under 「甲」: flipping the arbiter while the shape still loads would move `$expand`, import, seed and FK resolution from X to `sys_user` with neither a conversion nor a refusal in front of it, which is a silent runtime re-target. The dev's deviation is the correct reading; the flip is scoped into the 19.0 follow-up (item (2) of the dev's follow-up text), where it is a no-op once parse refuses the carrier.
3. **`Field.user()` TS surface: accept set and output unchanged.** `UserFieldInput = Omit<FieldInput, 'reference'> & { reference?: string }` is type-identical to `FieldInput` on that key (`FieldInput` is `Omit<Partial<Field>, 'type'>` and `Field.reference` is `string | undefined`); `@deprecated` is a doc annotation, not a narrowing. The spread stays last, so `Field.user({ reference: 'x' })` still emits `reference: 'x'`, and the lint sees it. **Right.** Moving `reference: 'sys_user'` after the spread would have been the silent re-target 「甲」 keeps out of 18.x; narrowing the type to `'sys_user'` would have been a compile-time refusal with no conversion. Both correctly left for 19.0.
4. **`@objectstack/lint` public surface widens:** a new rule id constant `USER_FIELD_FOREIGN_REFERENCE` (`'user-field-foreign-reference'`) exported from the barrel; a new `RULE_EXPLANATIONS` entry (so `os explain user-field-foreign-reference` resolves); and `validateObjectReferences` now returns a `warning` finding for a `user` field, on `objects` or `objectExtensions`, whose carrier is neither absent nor `sys_user`. It reaches `os validate` / `os build` / `os lint` through the existing reference-integrity suite in the authoring registry as an advisory, so no command's exit code changes (pinned per command by `splitBySeverity(runAuthoringRules(...))`). **Right:** this is the loud half 「甲」 rule 2 asks for, and the precedent for publishing a rule-id constant as a widening is `54d32e5147` (`Clause-②: yes (widening)` on the `os explain` landing). Two details read and accepted: the rule reads `referenceCarrierOf` (not `referenceTargetOf`), so an object-valued carrier still throws exactly as before (control test kept); interpolated targets are not exempted, which is correct because the type fixes the target. The `[#19289]` control that fed `reference: 'zzz_nope'` now expects both `object-reference-unknown` and the new warning: two different judgements on one field, right.
5. **The 「甲」 derivation (no ADR-0087 conversion can carry the refusal) holds on the cited code.** ADR-0087 D2 scopes conversions to lossless mappings (`0087:139`, semantic changes excluded `0087:152`). `user` is outside `DELETE_SEMANTICS_REFERENCE_TYPES = {master_detail, lookup, tree}` (`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts:1654`), `deleteBehavior` is `z.enum(['set_null','cascade','restrict'])` with no do-nothing value (`field.zod.ts:1637`), `fieldHoldsUsers` (`sharing-rule-service.ts:112`) branches on the type, and `current_user` is legal on `user` and on `lookup` only when the target is `sys_user` (`default-value-shape.ts:254`). So `user(X)` to `lookup(X)` changes delete semantics, sharing and a legal default: not lossless. **Right**; rule 2 applies, refusal is 19.0.
6. **In-repo producers.** Measured zero in `examples/**`, package source, `Field.user({ reference })` calls and YAML; two test fixtures. The object-graph module fixture `owner` is converted to `lookup` (line 42) and every other use of that fixture (`account.owner.email`, lines 63/121/171) resolves identically to `crm_person`. The "explicit carrier wins" control is rebuilt as an inline fixture that pins the protocol-18 resolution; `field-value.test.ts` keeps its pin. **Right:** the director's delta asked for producers to be converted, and a test that deliberately pins the 18.x resolution is not a producer; both pins carry a comment naming them as such and the follow-up lists them for retirement at 19.0.
7. **Generated and surface artifacts.** `UserFieldInput` is not exported, `packages/spec/api-surface-signatures.json` lists `FieldInput (type)` unchanged, and the head's `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Spec property liveness` and the Type Check jobs are green, so no regenerated artifact was owed. No governed surface (register row) is on the file list; the `Governed Surface Queue Guard` passed on the head.

The 18.x shape honours 「甲」: no silent narrowing (items 1, 3) and no silent runtime re-target (items 2, 3).

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/24808-user-field-foreign-reference-warning.md`: `@objectstack/lint: minor`, `@objectstack/spec: patch`. **Matches what the diff publishes.** lint publishes a new export, a new rule id and a new explain entry (a feature, `minor`); spec publishes a `@deprecated` annotation and docblocks only, with the accept set, output and runtime unchanged (`patch`). Not `skip-changeset` (two released packages publish). No `major`, no ADR-0087 marker owed (nothing breaks; `check:adr-0087-registration` reads no breaking changeset).

`Clause-②:` line: `yes (widening)` on the PR body and in the changeset, consistent with each other. The claim's provisional `no` was reset from the measurement, as the claim itself allowed; `yes` is right because a public rule-id constant and an explain entry are new public surface, and `(widening)` is the right arm because no accept set narrows. `yes` takes at least `minor`, which the lint entry carries.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev flags and `open_questions` from the os-dev-report (`6296320062`):

- **Open question 1 (`referenceTargetOf` flip, dispatch step 3):** answered. Option A (keep the authored-carrier-first resolution in 18.x; flip with the 19.0 refusal) is adopted; the dispatch's "either way" sentence is superseded by 「甲」 rule 2 for the reason in ① item 2. Not a defect of the PR.
- **Open question 2 (`Field.user` type narrowing):** answered. Option A (`@deprecated` now, narrow the type at 19.0) is adopted; ① item 3.
- **Out-of-scope finding 1 (the 19.0 follow-up card):** escalated to the `domain:spec` seat to file after this PR lands, with the dev's six-item scope (refusal at parse with the `tree` precedent, `referenceTargetOf` returns the constant, `Field.user` drops or narrows `reference`, the advisory's fate, the D3 semantic-migration entry plus a breaking changeset with `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` and its ADR-0087 marker, retirement of the three pins). Not blocking this landing.
- **Out-of-scope finding 2 (objectui `userCell.readGate-10535.test.tsx:157` renders `{ type: 'user', reference: 'crm_member' }`):** a renderer fixture, not a metadata producer; carrier is the 19.0 landing. Noted on the follow-up; not blocking.
- **Out-of-scope finding 3 (the advisory does not reach the object save door: the reference suite's runtime leg runs on `flow` / `dataset` snapshots only, `authoring-rules.ts`):** accepted as written. The 18.x loud half is owed at `os validate` / `os build` / `os lint`, which it reaches; crossing the suite onto `object` writes is that member's own false-positive measurement and belongs with the 19.0 card, not here.
- **NOT MEASURED (dev): the public `os validate` door through a built CLI binary; `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:lean-entry-closure` (prerequisite not met locally).** Covered by the head's check-runs: `Build Core`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates` and the Type Check jobs are green, and the registry path the CLI runs is pinned per command in the new describe.
- **Check-runs on the head (`38154076`):** 43 check-runs, all completed: 36 success, 7 skipped (opt-in and conditional jobs: 18.x upgrade harness, Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Dogfood Regression Gate, Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke, Temporal Conformance), 0 failure, none running. The six `Test Core` shards, `Build Core`, `Check Changeset`, both `Governed Surface Queue Guard` runs, every `Lint ·` and `Type Check ·` job and `Spec property liveness` are green. The head is green for landing.
